definition: The rule that refuses a hand-off of delegated work back up the line of hand-offs, to an agent that already handed the task down, so two agents cannot pass one task between them forever.
A grade for an enforcement mechanism, named by what an adversary would have to defeat to make the mechanism's claim false; there are five: Observed, Coordinated, Brokered, Confined and Attested.
The assurance mode in which the act may happen anywhere and the system keeps only best-effort evidence recorded afterwards, so there is nothing for an adversary to defeat.
The assurance mode in which cooperating clients declare their claims, roles, commitments and messages before acting, so an adversary need only decline to declare.
The assurance mode in which a chosen credential or effect channel passes through a broker the daemon owns, so an adversary must defeat that broker.
The assurance mode in which operating-system restrictions leave the process no other route to the protected effect, so an adversary must escape that confinement.
The assurance mode in which a key is released, or a result accepted, only to an environment whose measured build matches a published identity, so an adversary must subvert the measured environment.
